title: Impairments of Brain and Behavior: The Neurological Effects of Alcohol
abstract: Chronic alcohol consumption causes widespread damage to the brain. This article reviews the neurological effects of alcohol, including its impact on the frontal lobes, cerebellum, and limbic system, and discusses the cognitive and behavioral consequences of these changes.

title: Neurocircuitry in Alcoholism: A Substrate of Disruption and Repair
abstract: This review synthesizes findings on the neural substrates disrupted in alcoholism, including prefrontal, cerebellar, and pontine circuits, as well as white matter pathways. It also addresses brain recovery observed during sustained abstinence.

title: Neurocircuitry of Addiction
abstract: Drug addiction is a chronically relapsing disorder characterized by compulsion to seek and take the drug. This review discusses the neurocircuitry of addiction across three stages: binge/intoxication, withdrawal/negative affect, and preoccupation/anticipation, with emphasis on alcohol and other substances.

title: Mechanisms of Neurodegeneration and Regeneration in Alcoholism
abstract: This article reviews the mechanisms by which alcohol causes neurodegeneration, including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and excitotoxicity. It also examines the potential for neurogenesis and brain recovery during abstinence.

title: The Role of GABA in Alcohol Dependence and Withdrawal
abstract: This review focuses on the role of GABAergic signaling in the central amygdala and other brain regions in the development of alcohol dependence and the emergence of withdrawal symptoms, including anxiety and hyperexcitability.
